observations.seen: Frame 1 is a dim, blue-purple wash with no readable key direction despite the 'golden hour look' label. Frames 2 and 3 are flat and evenly lit. Frame 4 has the best night mood, with lamp posts, but the lamps cast little light onto the court.

Players get soft blob or contact shadows that are faint and mostly directionless. Frame 4 has some cast shadows near the bleachers, but there is no consistent sun or flood shadow direction across frames.
The court surfaces are matte with no sheen or reflections, even under the wet rain in frame 4. Only the trophy in frame 1 shows a metallic gold response.

The bleachers and ball cart are generic blocks. Backdrops are blurred photo-like planes (green interior, beige haze, treeline). The Venice palm floats unattached in the sky. Frame 1 has a giant pillar intersecting the court and the trophy oddly placed mid-court.
Frame 4 has light rain streaks and frame 2 has dust particles near the hoop. Frame 3's beige haze is flat fog that washes out the far background rather than adding depth.
Clothing is flat color with no fabric response. Skin is smooth unlit-looking. Court paint is uniform, with no wear or grain except a faint noise overlay.

The low-poly stylized characters are readable, but faces are simplistic and hands are mitten-like. The court line decals at the paint have broken white swoosh artifacts near the feet. The hoop and backboard are decent.

Frame 1 crops a player at the left edge and leaves a large empty foreground. Frames 2–4 cluster players mid-frame with the hoop cut off at the top right. The ball carrier is well emphasized by the orange ring.

Low perspective camera rather than the broadcast high angle. Frame 1 is very close and oblique with no clear court read. Frames 2–4 use a consistent shallow sideline angle that hides court layout depth.
There is background depth-of-field blur and a film grain or noise layer. Frame 1 is crushed and desaturated. There is no meaningful bloom on the lamps in frame 4.
The handler's dribble crouch varies across frames. Off-ball players stand in near-identical idle T-ish poses across all four shots. The players in frame 1 are mid-stride but stiff.
Frame 1 has a clean scoreboard, court tag, stamina bar and controls strip in a consistent orange/cyan style. The top mode bar is dense and debug-like, and frames 2–4 show no HUD at all.

nextChange.change: set the look's environment so metals/glossy materials pick up image-based reflections
